title: Guns and Robots
text: Oooh, Guns and Robots... It is such a shame how unpopular you are. Sure, you are not the greatest game out there, suffering a number of issues both big and small... But deep down there is a fun game here. Alas, what holds G&R back so hard is it's balancing and small, unsocial community. With any game that allows you to build your own weapon, there are bound to be dirty players who exploit this fact and abuse it to create frustrating builds that take the fun out of the game and either force you to build your own cheap build, or just attempt to tough it out and try your best to beat them (And if you have skills, chances are you will at the very least do a considerable amount of damage to their bot). As for the community, there is hardly anyone left... On average, there is probably around 150-100 players daily, if you are lucky.. Often this means fighting the same people over and over (said people probably being the cheap builds that frustrate you so), meaning it gets dull seeing the same robot over and over, nothing new and creative coming your way, and even worse for noobs to the game who get put together with level 80 vets. Even moreso, the community is very quiet for the most part, not much chattering going on between players, which further makes the game feel empty. Does this mean the game isn't worth playing? Hell naw, when I first started playing, I really enjoyed it. It is fun making your own personal robot that suits your playstyle, mixing and matching parts and painting them all up to make a fancy killing machine that people will easily remember and adore/fear, and when you join a guild, it is fun working together to gather enough money to help invest in the guild to purchase buffs that give you a slight edge against your rivals. That, and the fact that this is the most generous F2P game I played in a long time, where all the things you can buy with real money don't have serious impact in the game, keeping it fun for everyone. If you do plan on playing this, though, I suggest you bring some friends... It is much more fun when you have a crew you can rely on instead of having to go solo and risk having to be paired up with bots... yeah...

title: Guns of Icarus Online
text: This game has a lot of juicy mechanics I was looking forward to delving into… bad sadly this game just wasn’t fun for my group and I to play together. I think there is a lot of potential for a game like this, but Guns of Icarus just didn’t hit the mark. Compared with the dumbed down version of the same thing (4 people try to fly a ship together) we found ‘Lovers in a dangerous spacetime’ to be much more accessible and enjoyable. You can clearly see the repercussions of your actions, there is room to experiment and develop expertise, there are a few simple yet tough decisions which must be made at all times throughout the game, and there is room to communicate and work together as a team. Sure the skill ceiling is not as high but we at least enjoyed ourselves. Unfortunately we found playing this game to just be tedious most of the time. We would fly around for 5+ minutes looking for an AI ship to attack… then finally start combat and it was just everything going wrong at once. In its defense I’m sure this is very realistic simulation of war, but not really a fun one. Everyone knows what we need to do: kill the bad guy but how do I help this actually occure? As a pilot how do I know if I should be trying to retreat or press the attack or ram the other ship? Are we winning or losing? As an engineer is there anything else fun to do apart from just efficiently going between the balloon and the hull repairing them forever just so we don’t die? As a gunner should I just keep shooting and telling the pilot to keep the bad guy in my field of fire? All of this I am sure could be learnt with time but there is no fun way to progress through the learning curve. We ended up dropping this game very fast. Even playing online (if there were other players) we suspect that it would be just as un-satisfying. Either we would wipe the enemy ship in one clean blow thanks to good positioning Or we just get stuck going around and around in circles indefinitely as we did with the AI. Or more likely we just get wiped out by more experienced players with conceivable idea of how to grow or learn from our mistakes. So overall, this game has a great concept, it is well polished, has great mechanics but in my opinion just completely fails at providing good gameplay.

text: Hand of Fate is a unique combination of adventure/card/rogue-like with well done audio, and decent enough graphics.  The character you play as is a male warrior, so if you're hoping for a female character or a different style of character, this may not be the best game for you.  I give the game devs props for creating a card based game that is expanded, and pushes the envelope for a new style of game, and they did it well, but did they do it well enough? Each level is an individual dungeons where you follow a path of cards, at the end of which you fight that levels boss.  This game would more appropriately be titled 'Hand of Chance', as the random elements that make up a rogue-like combine with the card game elements to make an experience that relies more on the luck of the draw rather than skill or strategy. You start over on every level, and by that I mean you lose any items or money that you have, making every dungeon its own mission.  This negates the impact of dying, as you start the level fresh. The only loss you have would be of time spent playing. As to the equipment cards you have for your deck;  it is unlikely you will be able to play that perfect card you need or want during a typical dungeon; of the 28 cards I had in my collection, it would be generous to say that I  saw 10 during any one dungeon. Obviously you want to have more cards that are chosen based on what you enjoy, but overall the gear or weapons in your deck become less important, due to the small chance you will actually see them. Every level is randomly selected, which may give it a new look and feel as you progress forward, but it takes away control or any sense of power as there is no choice in where you go.  The randomization of what gear you may get combined with the random level you may end up on, and the random number of traps on that level can determine how well you do on a level.  The combat was not challenging; a matter of mashing the  mouse button and dodging when the green light flashes.  Skill and tactics play no part in the battles, only having the correct timing.  This gets quite boring very fast after a few battles. This game boils down to chance;  equipment, levels, perks, relics, weapons, traps, all is dependent upon the chance that you get the right one. There is no tactical challenge in this game; what combat there is is simplistic and offers no challenge.  If you're looking for a casual game, and like card games and rogue-likes, this may be for you, but if you're looking for a game based on skill rather than chance, I cannot recommend it. title: Hand of Fate
text: Excellent game with an incredibly interesting concept, and solid execution. Cards become your gear, encounters, everything, and many of them have tokens. By succeeding at that card's encounter, you get the token, which create new cards for future games. I'm playing the Story mode, and it's fantastic. I've progressively unlocked a bunch of different new stories that I'm encountering in future games. You choose your equipment and some of the encounter cards to build each match, and then the story setup you've selected adds cards. It's clever and works well. Most cards are choices rather than combat, with semi-random success, others are static choices that you can learn and rely on in future games. This creates a great mix of surprise and predictability. Combat is fairly basic but engaging - not the highlight of the game, but it doesn't hurt it either. Story mode (Guessing 6-8 hours playtime), endless-play mode, and then modifiers that change the way some things work.

I know how an exploding bold crossbow, and I have learned that many more items are destructable in the game than I had first imagined. Additionally, I learned that stones (which look like props) actually have ore and stuff inside of them. Nice surprise. Another really cool feature I noticed is that any enemy that you fight will drop any armor that they are wearing, also their weapons, and some additional loot. But it's cool to see that you get their actual items as loot. On top of that, you can break pieces of their armor off in battle, which is a nice little touch. Right now, I'm not sure if I'm supposed to have a goal in the game, so I've set myself the goal of collecting bloody goblin hearts from all my victims. Truth be told, I'm having a lot of fun with this game.

title: Hardland
text: What a great little game! A wonderfully unique art style which reminds me of Tim Burton and Wallace & Gromit, an absolute pleasure to behold all of the lovingly sculpted houses, characters, and environment! The enemies and environment vary sufficiently to keep me interested in them, the physics is a welcome feature, and the ground can be sculpted by explosions and magic impacts... very cool. The armour system is quite unique... on top of the usual durability points commonplace in RPGs, you will also find that pieces of armour can fly off when struck in combat! AWESOME The game was £10.99 when I bought it, this is fair I feel, considering the level of polish and content so far. So no criticism about the price. The only real criticism I have is currently the lack of narrative/story, and the lack of a tutorial system to ease new players into the game. While I realise this is in beta, it is not a trump card that can be played to excuse shortcomings. To wrap it up this is one of the most promising and unique RPGs I have seen in recent years. The charming art style, lovingly crafted locations, and good difficulty all provide a very solid foundation for what could be one of my favourite casual RPGs of all time. I really look forward to seeing future content they introduce to the game :)

text: Time to update this review. A substantial amount of work has been done since its early access release. Now this game is quite fun to play for extended periods of time. There is a lot to explore, quests available from townsfolk, random dungeons, monsters roaming the land. It is a very fun free-roaming sandbox arpg. Grand Theft Fable? The gameplay is pretty basic 3rd person arpg. Not isometric like Diablo et al, but presented in an over- the-shoulder 3rd person perspective like Fable(or GTA). You can be nice and help people, or you can steal from everybody and be a murderous thug. I am sure that at some point a story will be added, but right now it is more of a free-roaming sandbox. The combat is slightly loose, and could be tightened up a little bit. For the most part combat works as expected. Sometimes it is a little hard to time strikes perfectly. This is not bad enough to be a serious problem,  just a minor quibble with the gameplay which I'm sure can be adjusted. Even if they leave the combat as is, I'd still be happy with the game. But I could be  happier. I especially appreciate the graphics, which are slightly cute and cartoonish, yet stunning at the same time with the settings maxed out at 1080p. The developers are definitely working dilligently to complete the game. "Our goal is to make Hardland one of the great action adventure RPGs." "We want to make Hardland a world full of interesting characters, creatures, quests, and mysterious places. We will not dictate how you should play this game. We merely set the stage and let you make your own decisions. " I think the developers are well on their way to realizing those goals. Old review: This game is far from done. The art and graphics are great (see screenshots etc...), the gameplay is coming together(per developer 70% complete).  The game world, on the other hand, still has a way to go (per developer only 20% complete). When complete, I think it will be a great open world fantasy arpg. I would not buy this if you are looking for something you can put lots of hours into immediately. However if you want to support what I think will become a very fun game.... I can't wait to play this game when the gameworld is closer to 75% ready!
